Cadre 3.4.0 is a breaking MCP and template-efficiency release. It keeps human
governance explicit while reducing repeated context, response bytes, and tool
round trips.

## Smaller, honest MCP contract

- Reduces the public surface from 25 to 22 tools.
- Requires `mode: "prepare" | "apply"` on every approval-aware command and
  rejects missing, mixed, or unknown fields.
- Uses MCP resources for template discovery/individual reads and
  `template_get_many` for known bundles.
- Emits unchanged template bodies once as embedded resources; structured data
  contains descriptors and hashes rather than duplicate content.
- Returns compact apply receipts with status, digest/checkpoint, counts, and
  changed paths.

## Safe project-local candidate staging

- Moves unapproved candidates to `.cadre/stage/<candidate-id>/` and enforces
  `/stage/` in `.cadre/.gitignore` before files are written.
- Keeps `.cadre/init/*` invalid. Before initialization, `.cadre` may exist only
  as the bootstrap `.gitignore` plus `stage` shell.
- Replaces separate candidate manifest and staged-plan reads with one
  `candidate_inspect` call that validates exact files, hashes, safety limits,
  and an optional plan graph.
- Generates unchanged workflow/styleguide defaults inside initialization and
  binds generated defaults plus staged overrides into the approval digest.

## Compact v2 workflow and legacy upgrade safety

- Adds immutable template set v2 for new projects while preserving every
  published v1 template byte-for-byte.
- Reduces the project workflow from 30,545 bytes to 5,987 bytes. Durable
  authority, governance, safety, lifecycle, resumability, source-of-truth, and
  Git rules stay project-local; command procedures move to versioned skills.
- Splits implementation into a compact core with conditional parallel-worker,
  governed-mode, conflict, and recovery references.
- Reports `upgradeRequired` for v1 projects. Status, wisp, and explicit refresh
  remain available; other mutations fail with `PROJECT_REFRESH_REQUIRED`.
- Upgrades v1 only through a human-approved refresh containing the compact v2
  workflow, ignore rule, and runtime/template versions.

## Fewer execution calls

- `project_status` now provides project, track, and implementation views; one
  implementation view replaces separate project, graph, scheduler, and
  worktree preflight reads.
- Worktree creation records node start, integration records merge state, and
  cleanup records completion.
- Lost-response retries reconcile an existing worktree, merge commit, removed
  worktree, or missing journal transition.
- A normal delegated task uses four MCP calls. Governed integration uses a
  fifth call after human approval.

## Compatibility and upgrade

Direct MCP consumers must adopt the 3.4 tool names, scoped status views,
embedded template resources, compact receipts, and explicit adaptive modes.
Outstanding 3.3 proposal tokens must be prepared again.

```bash
npm install -g cadre-ai@3.4.0
cadre-ai doctor
cadre-ai install --target all --scope user
```

After upgrading, start a new Codex conversation and run `/reload-plugins` in
Claude Code. Existing projects should run Cadre `refresh` and explicitly
approve the v1→v2 proposal before further state mutation.

## Verification

- Frozen workspace installation with pnpm 11.4.0.
- Harness TypeScript check, 53 CLI/integration tests, package validation, and
  npm dry-run packing for `cadre-ai@3.4.0`.
- Complete docs content, lint, typecheck, and static production build.
- Local-build installation with `cadre@cadre` installed and enabled for Codex
  and Claude at their `3.4.0+*.local-20260827T052237Z` cache-buster versions.
- Regression budgets: tool catalog ≤18 KiB, workflow ≤6 KiB, common template
  and 50-item status results ≤4–8 KiB, and checkpoint/apply receipts ≤4 KiB.
- v1 template immutability, v2 generation/digest binding, legacy mutation
  gating, candidate path/symlink/size checks, adaptive schema rejection, and
  four/five-call worktree lifecycle coverage.
